narrative.what_i_did:
This session landed the spine of a mechanism the operator has been designing across many chats: an honest, tamper-evident record of trading moves, broadcast live so anyone can verify it. The idea is a standalone game he calls Beat the HODL Machine, where a person places a stake and then buys and sells chunks and races their result, in sats, against simply holding. The whole product only means anything if nobody can lie about when they moved or at what price, and he wanted that honesty to live in something reusable rather than bolted into one app. Importantly, he first pointed me at the wealth-strategy repo, I started building there, and he corrected me mid-turn to say this belongs somewhere else as its own mechanism for several ideas. I reverted that repo byte-for-byte, asked him in chip form where it should live, and he chose tapit-wallet. That is the right home, because tapit-wallet already holds the keys, already signs attestations, and already has a live Nostr transport it uses for sign-in, so the move chain rides rails that mostly exist instead of anything hand-rolled.

The cut is a new feature called move-chain, built entirely on top of tapit-attest with no new crypto. A move is an ordinary journal attestation minted through wallet.attest, and the chain is hash-linked on the library's own content address, envelopeId, exactly the way the succession primitive already links its records. The pure module, moveChain.ts, gives you buildMoveDraftInput to shape a move (the sequence number and the previous link live in the claim right next to the move's own payload, so both are covered by the signature and neither can be altered without breaking it), moveLink to get the address the next move chains on, readMoveMeta to read a move back, orderMoves to reassemble moves that arrived out of order, and verifyMoveChain, which is the load-bearing part. verifyMoveChain is all-or-nothing on purpose: every move has to carry a valid signature from the chain owner's own identity so nobody can claim someone else's chain, name the same owner as the genesis, sit at a sequence exactly equal to its position, and link its previous hash to the real address of the move before it, with the genesis carrying sequence zero and an empty previous. Any hole, any reorder, any edited move, or anyone stamping a foreign identity as the subject all read as invalid. It is covered by fourteen tests that mint real signed chains with a throwaway wallet and then try to cheat them.

The live broadcast is a second small module, moveChannel.ts, sitting in the transport feature exactly like the liveness channel does. It rides its own public wire kind, ninety-five eighty-four, and unlike the encrypted inbox and the liveness channel it is deliberately unencrypted and unaddressed, because the entire point of a move is that the world can read and verify it. publishMove wraps a signed move as a Nostr event through the existing buildEvent seam, so the private key never crosses the boundary, and subscribeMoves verifies the outer event, parses and structurally validates the inner move, re-checks the inner signature, and binds the broadcaster to the author so a relay or a stranger cannot inject a move under a foreign name. It is covered by seven tests against a fake transport that records what gets published and replays events back into the subscriber, which exercises the whole channel except the one thing this sandbox physically cannot do, which is reach a real relay. All six gates are green: typecheck, lint, the full suite at nine hundred twenty-four tests, build with the bundle budgets satisfied, the test baseline ratcheted up to ninety-seven files, and the doctrine check. It landed as commit af39b0e on the working branch, not on main.

The second cut, commit 936253b, is the truth scorer, which is the part the operator keeps calling the heart of it: your math shows the truth. He tightened the rules to whole coin, all in or all out. You start holding one whole bitcoin, and your only moves are to sell the whole coin and buy the whole coin back, over and over. So the scorer, truthScore.ts, replays a chain of sell and buy-back switches against the prices they were stamped at, charges friction on every single leg, and reports your coin count now against the HODL ball, which is a fixed one point zero that never moves. It also reports the coins you gave up to friction as an honest counterfactual, the same moves run frictionless minus the real run, each round's contribution, and, while you are sitting in cash after a sell, exactly how low the price has to drop for you to buy back and beat the ball. An out-of-turn move, like selling when you are already in cash, is skipped and flags the run rather than corrupting the count. It is eleven tests, including the case he described himself, where two good round trips turn one coin into four. A second decision he made this session is baked into the shape: the donation or stake is not a gate and not part of the math. Anyone plays for free and still sees they cannot beat the ball; the stake is only how seriously the world takes a claim, a dollar taken as a dollar's worth of seriousness. So the scorer is stake-agnostic, coin count against one, and any credibility layer sits beside it, never inside it.
narrative.whats_pending:
Three honest threads remain before this is a thing the operator can hold in his hand. The first is the live relay round-trip, which I could not verify from here at all. The channel logic is fully tested against a fake transport, but whether a real move actually propagates to damus, nos.lol, primal and the rest needs a device smoke: publish a move and watch the topic feed, or the wallet's npub, in a Nostr client. Until that happens, the broadcast is proven correct in shape but unproven on the wire.

The second is that there is no UI surface yet, by choice. This cut is the primitive and the channel, the way the liveness feature shipped its primitive and its channel before it was ever mounted. Nothing imports these modules, so they add nothing to the bundle and change nothing a user sees. The arena screen, where a person places a rock, buys and sells, and watches their chain go live against the HODL line, is the next cut and it is where this becomes visible.

The third is the genesis-of-chain idea from the design chats, which is the part that ties a move chain to an entry or a donation transaction so the chain literally begins at a real on-chain event. The move-chain primitive is deliberately generic about what the genesis is, so that wiring is a clean addition rather than a rework. Also parked as a deliberate v1 simplification: verifyMoveChain binds a chain to a single un-rotated identity, and honoring a key rotation partway through a chain, using the succession primitive that already exists here, is a later refinement rather than a gap.
narrative.what_you_could_do_better:
The most useful thing to record is the near-miss on where this got built. I began cutting the same mechanism inside the wealth-strategy repo, added a dependency and files there, and only stopped when the operator corrected me. I reverted it cleanly and nothing landed, but the lesson is that a mechanism described as reusable and standalone should have prompted me to ask where it lives before I touched any repo, not after. The chip-form question I eventually asked is exactly the one I should have led with.

On the code itself, one judgment worth a second look is the choice to broadcast moves fully public and unencrypted on their own kind. That is right for a game whose whole value is public verifiability, and it matches how a kind-one note is public by design, but if a future idea on this same primitive wants private-until-revealed chains, the channel will need an encrypted sibling rather than a change in place. I would not pre-build that now, but it is the obvious next fork. The other honest note is that the identity binding in verifyMoveChain is strict enough that a rotated wallet mid-chain would read as invalid today; that is a safe default for v1 and I flagged it, but it is a real edge a long-lived chain will eventually hit.
narrative.bigger_picture:
This connects straight to the wall this repo is built around. An attestation expresses intent and can never move a coin; a spend signature moves a coin and is never an attestation. A trading move is pure intent, so it sits squarely on the safe side, and that is exactly why the move chain could be built entirely on the existing attestation primitive without going anywhere near the money-touching bridge that the previous session left as a staged, parity-gated plan. The mechanism teaches the same thing the product does: your record is only as good as an unbroken, signed chain you cannot secretly edit, which is the honest inverse of every trading track record on the internet.

The deeper point is that this is the wallet earning its role as the hub. The operator wanted one honest mechanism that several ideas can ride, and by putting it here it inherits the keys, the signing, and the live transport for free, and any future idea that needs a signed, ordered, publicly-verifiable log of moments gets it by supplying its own payload. Beat the HODL Machine is the first rider, not the thing itself. If it only ever works for one family it has already succeeded, and the reason it can work at all is that the hard parts, the signing and the chaining and the wire, were already sitting in this repo waiting to be pointed at a new idea.

feedback_to_appcommander: One reinforcement worth lifting: when the operator describes a mechanism as reusable and standalone, ask WHERE it lives before touching any repo, not after. I started cutting this inside a sibling app and had to revert cleanly when he corrected me; a chip-form 'which repo' up front would have avoided the false start. The build itself confirmed the tapit-attest primitive is genuinely reusable for non-identity ideas — a trading move is just a journal attestation chained on envelopeId, no new crypto — which is a good signal that the 'one envelope standard' is paying off beyond the wallet's original scope. Also a small environment note for any dispatched tapit-wallet session: a fresh clone must build the vendored bip341-psbt-signer (npm --prefix bip341-psbt-signer run build) before typecheck reads clean, since plain typecheck does not run prebuild; without it the sign-request feature shows module-not-found errors that are purely a build-order artifact, not real failures.
